text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
English poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson was born in 1809.
Australian novelist Rolf Boldrewood, who wrote "Robbery Under Arms" was born in 1826.
Australia's first native-born Governor General, Sir Isaac Isaacs, was born near Albury in 1855. He entered the Victorian Parliament in 1892 and was Governor-General for five years from 1931.

The discoverer of penicillin, Sir Alexander Fleming, was born in 1881. The Scottish bacteriologist won a Nobel Prize for medicine in 1945 with Howard Florey and Ernest Chain for his important invention.
One of the most loved actresses and television comedy pioneers, Lucille Ball, was born in 1910. She played a dumb redhead in her series "I Love Lucy" but was a whizz at business. She died in 1989.
American actor, Robert Mitchum, was born in 1917. He came to Australia to appear in "The Sundowners".
**EVENTS**
1623 : Anne Hathaway, wife of English dramatist and poet
William Shakespeare, died.
1660 : Diego Velazquez, Spanish painter, died. He became
a major figure of 17th century art and was famed for his realism. Among his most famous works are "Las Maninas" (Maids of Honour) and "Venus and Cupid".
1825 : Bolivia was proclaimed an independent republic
after nearly 300 years of Spanish rule.
1879 : The first night game of Australian Rules Football

was played at the Melbourne Cricket Ground under a "stream of electricity". The game between Collingwood Artillery and East Melbourne drew 12,000 spectators but the lighting was inadequate and the 'special white ball' burst.
1890 : The electric chair was used for the first time.
Convicted murderer William Kemmler was executed at New York.
1914 : Austria-Hungary declared war on Russia and Serbia
declared war on Germany.
1915 : Fresh allied landings of 25,000 men at Suvla Bay
on the Gallipoli Peninsula failed; 252,000 allied troops were casualties of the Gallipoli campaign between 1915-1916.
1918 : In World War One the second battle of the Marne
ended. In what was the last German attack on the Western Front they suffered at least 100,000 casualties.
1926 : American gold medallist swimmer, Gertrude Ederle,
became the first woman to swim the English Channel. The 20-year-old New Yorker completed the 56 kilometre swim in 14 hours, 31 minutes.
1928 : Andy Warhol, U.S. artist and a pioneer of pop art,
born.
1931 : The New South Wales State Treasury said it didn't
have the money to pay public servants their salaries.
1945 : The Japanese city of Hiroshima was devastated and

at least 140,000 people were killed when the atomic bomb was dropped. U.S. President Harry Truman decided to use the destructive bomb to end the Second World War.Three days later the Americans bombed Nagasaki, to force Japan's surrender.
1951 : National Service training began in Australia.
Intakes all over the country began their 98 days of compulsory service.
1962 : Jamaica became independent after 300 years of
British rule.
1971 : Round-the-world yachtsman Chay Blyth completed his

48,000 kilometre trip in the record-breaking time of 292 days. Twice during the voyage he was almost washed overboard from his all-steel ketch "British Steel". For much of the trip the 31-year-old sailed without the benefit of the self-steering gear, which was broken in a storm.
1973 : Blind American musician Stevie Wonder was
seriously injured in a car accident.
1978 : Pope Paul VI died of a heart attack. Six days
later, 200,000 people attended Pope Paul's funeral.
1988 : Russian ballerina Natalia Makarova danced with the
Kirov Ballet for the first time since defecting 18 years earlier.
1990 : U.N. Security Council voted 13-0 to ban trade with
Iraq except for medicine and some food for humanitarian relief after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait.
1990 : Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was thrown
out of office by the military.
1993 : Mirihito Hosokawa became Prime Minister of Japan.
1996 : U.S. scientists revealed they had found evidence
of ancient life on Mars in remnants of a meteorite discovered in Antarctica.
